item.title: PID Control Optimization and Trajectory Tracking for Autonomous Differential Drive Robots
item.description:
We built a non-linear PID controller with moving integral windows, velocity-dependent target yaws, and anti-windup limits. We compared A* and Dijkstra path generation and modeled LiDAR obstacle avoidance in ROS GazeboSim.

We validated the controller at the Emil Buehler Aerospace Lab with TurtleBot Vicon motion capture and matched-pairs tests at p < 0.01. The results supported the use of low-cost autonomous differential-drive hardware.
